ideas.hypothesis: In EU new member states, expenditure-based fiscal consolidations raise export growth through wage moderation, an internal-devaluation channel. The export response should therefore be stronger under fixed exchange-rate regimes and should run through falls in unit labour costs.

sources.role: finding and method: panel identification of fiscal shocks in NMS; investment and exports rise and wages fall after expenditure-based consolidation
setting: Romania as a small open economy with a flexible exchange rate
measure: structural deficit and fiscal impulse

ideas.test: Quarterly panel of 10 NMS, 1999-2015: identify consolidation shocks (narrative or SVAR) and estimate local projections of export growth and unit labour costs, interacting the shocks with exchange-rate regime (euro or peg vs float). Test mediation through unit labour costs.
ideas.disconfirming: Export responses are the same across regimes, exports rise with no fall in unit labour costs, or the response vanishes once foreign demand is controlled.

ideas.hypothesis: Across European emerging economies, fiscal multipliers fall systematically with trade openness and exchange-rate flexibility. Small open floaters like Romania should have cumulative spending multipliers well below 0.5, while less open peggers have multipliers near 1.

sources.role: finding: low impact and cumulative multipliers in Romania, attributed to openness and a flexible exchange rate
method: several shock-identification methods with panel estimation for NMS
setting: relative effectiveness of fiscal and monetary policy in Serbia

ideas.test: Panel SVAR or local projections for about 15 CEE and Balkan countries, 2000-2019, with spending shocks identified Blanchard-Perotti style. Interact shocks with openness (imports/GDP) and regime dummies and report impact and cumulative multipliers by group.
ideas.disconfirming: Multipliers do not differ significantly by openness or regime, or more open economies have larger multipliers.

ideas.hypothesis: Better institutions make fiscal policy less procyclical, and the effect is strongest in resource-rich Sub-Saharan African countries, where weak institutions turn commodity booms into spending booms. As institutions improve within a country, the correlation between government spending and the output gap should fall.

sources.role: finding and method: procyclical fiscal policy in SSA and its structural determinants (institutional quality, resource abundance, fragility)
measure: assessing cyclical stance via structural deficit and fiscal impulse
method: testing for structural change in how fiscal policy is conducted

ideas.test: Panel of about 45 SSA countries, 1980-2018: estimate time-varying cyclicality coefficients of real primary spending on the output gap. Regress them on ICRG/WGI institutional indices interacted with resource rents/GDP, with country fixed effects and terms-of-trade instruments for the cycle.
ideas.disconfirming: Improvements in institutional quality within countries are not followed by less procyclical spending, or the interaction with resource rents is null.

ideas.hypothesis: Fiscal multipliers are larger when monetary policy accommodates (policy rate held fixed, at the zero lower bound, or under a peg) than when the central bank leans against the fiscal impulse. The strategic interaction in Nash-equilibrium policy models should therefore show up in state-dependent SVAR responses.

sources.role: mechanism: BMW model of strategic interaction between central bank and fiscal authority (Nash equilibrium, interest-rate and investment traps)
method: SVAR with output, inflation, monetary policy, fiscal revenue and expenditure
finding: the monetary stance conditions the macroeconomic effects of consolidations
setting: estimating fiscal vs monetary effectiveness in a small economy

ideas.test: State-dependent SVAR or local projections for a panel of OECD and emerging economies. Identify spending shocks and estimate two-year cumulative multipliers in regimes defined by the policy-rate response (Taylor-rule residual) and by ZLB episodes.
ideas.disconfirming: Multipliers in accommodative regimes are no larger than in non-accommodative ones, or the difference disappears once the public debt level is controlled.

ideas.hypothesis: Fiscal consolidations whose timing and composition are uncertain to private agents depress private investment more than equally sized consolidations announced as credible multi-year plans. Measured fiscal-policy uncertainty should therefore amplify the output cost of consolidation.

sources.role: mechanism: uncertainty over the timing and composition of consolidation shapes whether it is expansionary
finding: investment response to consolidation shocks
method: medium-term budget forecasting and planning as a way to reduce uncertainty

ideas.test: Combine narrative consolidation episodes for OECD countries (1978-2014) with news-based fiscal policy uncertainty indices. Run local projections of private investment and GDP on consolidation size interacted with pre-consolidation uncertainty and with whether a medium-term fiscal framework exists.
ideas.disconfirming: The size x uncertainty interaction is insignificant, or high-uncertainty consolidations cost no more output than credible pre-announced ones.

ideas.hypothesis: Countries with larger automatic stabilizers (higher budget semi-elasticity to the output gap) enacted smaller discretionary stimulus in 2008-09 but did not suffer larger output declines. This would mean automatic stabilizers substitute for discretionary policy, with shorter decision lags and less political distortion.

sources.role: mechanism: automatic stabilizers as a faster, politically shielded alternative to discretionary policy
setting: fiscal policy responses abroad in the 2008-09 crisis
mechanism: limits of countercyclical fiscal policy in the USA
setting: G20 stimulus packages in 2008-09

ideas.test: Cross-section of about 35 OECD/G20 countries: measure stabilizer size with OECD budget semi-elasticities and discretionary packages with IMF/OECD 2008-10 estimates. Regress package size and peak-to-trough GDP decline on stabilizer size, controlling for pre-crisis debt, financial exposure and exchange-rate regime.
ideas.disconfirming: Stabilizer size is unrelated to package size, or countries with large stabilizers suffered larger output losses given the shock.

ideas.hypothesis: Budget-process reforms (fiscal rules, top-down budgeting, stronger finance ministries) come later and less often under proportional representation without government alternation. External anchors such as the Maastricht convergence deadlines weaken this political barrier.

sources.role: mechanism and setting: timing of Italian budget reform depends on party system, alternation and electoral rules; Europeanization
setting: Maastricht design and fiscal constraints
mechanism: components of budget process reform and obstacles to adoption

ideas.test: Panel of EU-15 plus NMS, 1980-2015: hazard model for adoption of budget-institution reforms (coded from fiscal-rule and budgetary-institution indices) on electoral system, history of government alternation (party-government data), and their interaction with Maastricht/accession deadlines.
ideas.disconfirming: Reform hazards are not lower under PR without alternation, or the external-anchor interaction is absent.

ideas.hypothesis: R&D tax incentives raise innovation output more than direct R&D grants of equal fiscal cost among firms that already do market R&D, because the two are complements. Grants should matter more for firms with no prior R&D.

sources.role: finding and mechanism: in a growth model calibrated to China, tax incentives complement market R&D and have larger growth effects than R&D grants

ideas.test: Chinese firm panel (2008-2015) linking tax-incentive eligibility (the R&D-intensity threshold for high-tech enterprise certification) and grant receipt to patents and new-product sales. Regression discontinuity at the eligibility threshold with heterogeneity by prior R&D status, plus matched comparison of grant recipients per yuan of support.
ideas.disconfirming: Tax-incentive effects on patents are no larger for prior R&D performers, or grants outperform tax incentives per yuan for that group.

ideas.hypothesis: Wars financed mainly by money creation and short-term notes rather than taxes cause structural breaks in which the government departs from its intertemporal budget constraint. Countries that tax-financed a larger share of war spending return to a sustainable fiscal reaction function sooner.

sources.role: finding: Confederate reliance on treasury notes and bonds with little tax revenue ended in fiscal failure
method: tests of intertemporal budget constraint consistency and structural breaks over a century of Australian fiscal data

ideas.test: Long-run annual fiscal series covering war episodes (Australia since 1901, US Union and Confederacy, UK). Estimate Bohn-type fiscal reaction functions with endogenous break dates, then relate post-war reaction coefficients and time to sustainability to the tax-financed share of war spending.
ideas.disconfirming: The tax share of war finance is unrelated to break timing or post-war sustainability, or money-financed wars show no departure from the intertemporal budget constraint.

ideas.hypothesis: EU member states in the high energy- and environmental-tax cluster cut the energy intensity of GDP faster without slower GDP growth, so energy taxation moves countries onto a decoupled growth path.

sources.role: method and setting: hierarchical clustering of EU-28 countries by energy, environmental, transport and pollution tax shares
mechanism: green fiscal measures, recovery and fiscal deficits

ideas.test: Eurostat environmental tax and energy statistics for EU-28, 2000-2019: cluster countries on 2000-2005 tax shares, then compare 2005-2019 energy-intensity declines and GDP growth across clusters. Complement with a panel regression of energy intensity on implicit energy tax rates with country and year fixed effects.
ideas.disconfirming: High-tax clusters do not reduce energy intensity faster, or they grow significantly more slowly.
